subject: Future Tech
title: Imagined Movement Detection
description: A short lesson to help you apply Imagined Movement Detection.

hook.text: You don't have to actually move for a BCI to work. Just imagining a movement creates detectable brain signals.

buildup.text: Motor imagery activates the same cortical areas as real movement, just without the final command to muscles.

discovery.text: EEG-based BCIs exploit this. Imagining left-hand movement creates a pattern different from right-hand imagery.

twist.text: Not everyone can produce clear motor imagery. About 15% of users struggle, a problem called BCI illiteracy.

climax.text: Training and neurofeedback help most users improve. The brain learns to produce signals the BCI can detect.

punchline.text: Imagining the move is enough to make it happen.

quiz.question: What is 'BCI illiteracy'?
options: Difficulty producing clear motor imagery signals
